finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::sql statement injection: validateselectquery validates a comment-stripped copy of the query, but executequery interpolates the original string into a simple-protocol query, so ddl/dml can be smuggled past the read-only guard

verdict.reasoning: I traced the payload through both files as supplied. sql-validator.ts strips `--...` to end-of-line with a regex that is unaware of double-quoted identifiers, and every subsequent check (first token, FORBIDDEN_KEYWORDS loop, `;` split) runs only on that stripped copy, while datasource.service.ts:148 interpolates the untouched `dto.query` into `SELECT * FROM (${dto.query}) AS _q LIMIT 10001`. For `SELECT 1 AS "x--" ) AS q; DROP TABLE users; SELECT * FROM (SELECT 1`, the validator sees only `SELECT 1 AS "x` (passes all checks), whereas Postgres treats `--` inside the double-quoted identifier as literal text and receives three complete statements; node-postgres sends a value-less string via the simple query protocol, which does execute multiple `;`-separated statements. The claim also correctly notes this is pre-existing and untested (sql-validator.spec.ts only covers the naive `SELECT 1; DROP TABLE users` case), and nothing in this diff closes it.

finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::tls certificate verification permanently disabled for datasource connections (`rejectunauthorized: false`), so "ssl enabled" gives no mitm protection for credentials or query data

verdict.reasoning: In packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts, `createClient` builds the pg Client with `ssl: ds.sslEnabled ? { rejectUnauthorized: false } : false` (the same object literal the diff modifies by adding `types`), and the decrypted password is passed in the adjacent `password: decrypt(ds.password)` line. With `rejectUnauthorized: false` and no CA/servername configured, node-postgres/TLS accepts any certificate, so enabling SSL yields encryption without server authentication — a MITM can present a self-signed cert and capture credentials and query results. The claim is accurate about the code as written; I could not run the repo-wide grep (no checkout is mounted) to confirm there is no CA-pinning path elsewhere, but nothing in the supplied datasource files provides one. Note the weakness is pre-existing rather than introduced by this diff, which only adds the `types` parser option.

finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.service.ts::ssrf / internal port scanning: user-supplied host+port are connected to with no allowlist, and raw driver errors are returned to the caller, making the backend an oracle for the internal network

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the supplied files: CreateDataSourceDto only length/range-validates host and port with no address denylist, and createClient (datasource.service.ts, the `new Client({ host: ds.host, port: ds.port, ... })` block the diff touches to add `types`) dials whatever the user supplies. testConnection returns `{ success: false, error: (error as Error).message }` and executeQuery rethrows `pgError.message` in a BadRequestException, so raw driver errors (ECONNREFUSED vs. timeout vs. protocol error) do reach the authenticated caller — a working internal port-scan oracle, exactly as claimed. The claim misreads nothing; my only qualifications are that the routes are gated by JwtAuthGuard plus workspaceService.assertMember (so it is not unauthenticated), and that this is entirely pre-existing and inherent to a user-configured Postgres connector, with the leak limited to connection-level signals rather than response bodies. Hence real, but I rate it minor.
